title: PMOVES.AI — Architecture Walkthrough
subtitle: A local-first, event-driven AI platform — in standard systems terms first
summary: A three-minute tour of what PMOVES.AI is as an engineering system: specialized agents coordinated over an event bus, hybrid retrieval, model routing, observability, and human-approval gates — moved from scattered experiments to a bounded, observable, production-shaped platform. The distinctive internal names come last, once the conventional architecture is clear.

sections.heading: 1 — The system in one breath
sections.body: PMOVES.AI is a local-first, event-driven platform that coordinates specialized AI agents to do real work. In conventional terms: an orchestration layer routes tasks to agents; agents call retrieval, tools, and models; results pass through logging, evaluation, and human-approval gates before they count. The whole thing runs on infrastructure the operator owns — not a rented API surface.

sections.heading: 2 — How the pieces fit
sections.body: A runtime orchestration and routing layer selects the right workspace for a task and binds each agent to a model, persona, tool set, and policy. Agents exchange structured context over an event bus instead of ad-hoc calls. Retrieval is hybrid — vector, graph, and full-text fused — so answers are grounded. A model gateway routes across providers by cost, capability, and availability, with a local-GPU floor so the lights stay on offline.

sections.heading: 3 — Trust and provenance
sections.body: Every agent has a cryptographic identity, and every consequential action writes a signed, non-repudiable audit trail. State travels as compact structured packets on the event bus, so what an agent knew and did is reviewable after the fact. This is the difference between a demo and a system you can put in front of an auditor: outputs are traceable to inputs, identities, and approvals.

sections.heading: 4 — From prototype to production
sections.body: The platform is built to cross the gap most AI work never does. Evaluation harnesses score representative tasks; human-review gates hold anything consequential; Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, and ClickHouse make behavior observable; and a layered, sovereign egress keeps the mesh private and self-hosted. New work moves through explicit lifecycle stages — rehearsal, live, review, archive — rather than shipping straight to users.

sections.heading: 5 — Now the internal names
sections.body: With the conventional architecture in view, the distinctive vocabulary lands cleanly: workspaces are 'rooms on a stage'; the orchestrator is 'P7'; the model/persona/tool bindings are 'suits'; the structured-context event exchange is the 'Geometry Bus'; the cryptographic identity and signed trails are 'CHIT'; and the whole is a 'Metal-Organic Framework' — every node a pore in one lattice. Same engineering, memorable names.
